speedkit/settings.py (every function below that changes files is a dry run by default and returns a plan dict; a real run needs dry_run=False, goes through a Journal and raises JournalError while TS4_x64.exe runs):
- graphics_status(sims=SIMS, game_bin=GAME_BIN) -> dict. Keys: active ('stock'|'simp_sgr_full'|'simp_setters'|'simp_other'|'other'), label, preset, rules_file, files (ConfigOverride files, each marked loaded or not), levels (from Options.ini), differences [{prop, what, stock, active, effect heavier/lighter/different, plain}], missing_stock_options, config_log {first_line, matches, newer_than_rules}, notes, heavier, lighter.
- graphics_use_stock(dry_run=True, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True) -> plan. Quarantines every .sgr in ConfigOverride. Journal kind 'settings'.
- graphics_use_preset(name='Ultimate Performance', dry_run=True, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True, source=None, game_bin=GAME_BIN) -> plan.
  - Copies GraphicsRules.sgr and SimpsSetters.sgr from <Sims 4>\Simps_GraphicsRules_Setters, plus the chosen preset's MySetters.sgr, into ConfigOverride.
  - Uses Journal.put_new for new files and Journal.replace for changed ones; identical files are skipped.
  - Preset names are case-insensitive: Ultimate Performance, Ultimate Quality, With Distance Blur, Defaults. An unknown name raises ValueError.
  - The plan includes a 'preview' of the differences from stock that the preset would give.
- graphics_restore(journal_id, dry_run=True, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True) -> list of actions (journal.undo).
- list_presets(sims=SIMS, source=None) -> {name: MySetters.sgr path}.
- compare_rules(stock_rules, active_rules, levels) -> list of differences.
- options_status(sims=SIMS, preset='balanced') -> {path, exists, settings [{key, label, value, meaning, cost, suggested?, suggested_meaning?}], notes}.
- options_apply(preset='balanced'|'performance', dry_run=True, display='auto'|'keep'|'fullscreen'|'borderless'|'windowed', extra=None, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True) -> plan {changes [{key, label, old, new, old_meaning, new_meaning}], journal, game_running, ...}.
  - Rewrites only the listed keys; every other byte of Options.ini stays identical.
  - A key missing from the file is appended in the game's own style.
  - Refuses while the game runs. Values are checked, so they cannot inject extra lines.
- read_options(sims=SIMS) -> {key: value}.
- caches_status(sims=SIMS) -> {caches [{name, path, files, bytes, what, when}], parked_old_caches, note}.
- caches_clean(which=('localthumbcache',), dry_run=True, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True) -> plan.
  - Quarantines only the 5 known caches: localthumbcache, localsimtexturecache, avatarcache, cachestr, onlinethumbnailcache. Journal kind 'caches'.
  - Folders stay in place; only their files move.
  - Any other name raises ValueError. It refuses anything inside saves, Tray, Options.ini, UserSetting.ini, accountDataDB, notify.glob, content, ConfigOverride, Mods, Mods_parked or SpeedKit.
- restore(journal_id, dry_run=True, sims=SIMS, home=None, check_game=True) -> actions. Generic undo.
- journals(sims=SIMS, home=None) -> this component's journals.
- preflight(sims=SIMS, processes=True, top=10) -> {memory {ram_total_mb, ram_available_mb, commit_used_mb, commit_limit_mb, load_percent}, pagefiles, top_processes, apps [{name, count, private_mb, system, service}], disk {C, E}, game_running, parked {files, bytes, manifest_items, lean}, last_start_free_mb, graphics, warnings [plain str], notes, ok}.
  - Read-only. It never kills or closes anything.
- memory_status() -> RAM and commit charge (GlobalMemoryStatusEx).
- process_memory() -> ({processes, pagefiles}, source). One PowerShell call (Get-Process + Win32_PageFileUsage); falls back to tasklist.
- main(argv) CLI: python -m speedkit.settings status|graphics|options|caches|preflight|journals|use-stock|use-preset <name>|options-apply [preset] [display]|caches-clean [names]|restore <id>. Nothing changes without --apply.

speedkit/settings_sgr.py:
- evaluate(path, machine=None, include_overrides=None) -> Rules. Runs a GraphicsRules.sgr script and what it includes. include_overrides={'MySetters.sgr': path} previews a preset.
- Rules.effective(levels) -> {prop: (value, where)} at the given Options.ini levels.
- Rules also exposes .vars, .options, .globals, .files, .missing, .info (logSystemInfo lines), .undefined, .errors.
- machine_vars(config_log) -> machine variables read from Config.log.
- fmt(v) -> a value formatted as it would appear in a prop.

speedkit/launch.py:
- launch(exe=GAME_EXE, dry_run=True, args=(), sims=SIMS, home=None, profile=None, check_game=True, processes=True) -> {started, dry_run, exe, args, profile, profile_source, launch_file, pid, preflight, warnings, refused}.
  - Runs preflight first. Refuses if TS4 already runs or the exe is missing.
  - Starts the exe detached: DETACHED_PROCESS, a new process group, and breakaway from the caller's job when Windows allows it.
  - Writes <Sims 4>\SpeedKit\launch_time.json {epoch, iso, profile, profile_source, exe, args, pid}.
- detect_profile(sims=SIMS, home=None) -> (profile, source). SpeedKit\profile_state.json wins; otherwise 'lean'/'full' from Mods_parked\_manifest.json.
- main(argv) CLI: python -m speedkit.launch [--apply].

Attribution charges a mod for game code it calls. A mod that wraps a busy game function (a common injection pattern) is charged for that function; the report's self% column separates the two cases. Mods whose code is not in sys.modules with a .ts4script __file__, and whose co_filename lacks '.ts4script', count as 'game'.
Stacks deeper than 100 frames are cut by CPython, so a mod frame below frame 100 is missed. Samples are taken only from the main thread, identified by the thread id at the time of the cheat.

Stopping a run parses the dump on the simulation thread: about 0.4-1.0 s per 1,500 samples of 100-frame stacks, measured in the game's Python. Runs are capped at 12,000 samples, so the pause stays under about 4 s.

CC guard: the lookup is proven in the running game through WickedWhims's log. What is not proven is whether outfit part_ids still hold unknown ids after a load. If the game strips them while loading, the guard finds nothing. It checks only the active household's outfits in their current occult form.
The Zone.update wrapper is installed at the first speedkit.lag and never removed (by design, so later wrappers stay chained). When no measurement is running it does one global check per tick.

findings.what: The dry run of restore()/graphics_restore() is the default, and it is what the CLI 'settings restore <id>' runs without --apply. It raised JournalError for every journal that replaces a file, which means every use-preset and options-apply run. The cause is in journal.undo(dry_run=True): it does not simulate its own put_new removal, so the quarantined original always looks blocked ('something is in its place').
findings.evidence: The new test test_restore_of_replace_journal_is_not_refused failed before the fix with: speedkit.journal.JournalError: cannot restore ...\ConfigOverride\MySetters.sgr: something is in its place. The builder's tests only ever called restore with dry_run=False on replace journals, so they never hit this.
findings.fix: Added settings._undo_plan(), which walks the journal steps newest first and tracks which paths each step frees or fills. restore() (and so graphics_restore) now returns this simulated plan for the dry run and no longer calls journal.undo(dry_run=True). The real run still goes through journal.undo. The root cause stays in journal.py, which I was told not to edit.

findings.what: journal.undo checks whether a restore target is free only when it reaches that step. When a later step conflicts, the earlier files have already been moved back and the journal stays 'committed'. A second undo then refuses with 'quarantined copy is missing', so the run can no longer be undone without manual moves.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with test_restore_refuses_before_moving_anything_when_a_path_is_taken: after use_stock, a new GraphicsRules.sgr was placed in ConfigOverride. Before the fix, graphics_restore moved MySetters.sgr and SimpsSetters.sgr back and then raised on GraphicsRules.sgr, leaving ConfigOverride as ['GraphicsRules.sgr','MySetters.sgr','SimpsSetters.sgr'].
findings.fix: settings.restore() now runs _undo_plan first and raises JournalError listing every problem before anything moves. Once the conflict is gone, undo works. Root cause reported for journal.py.

findings.what: tests/test_settings.py built its fixture from the user's live Options.ini, ConfigOverride and Config.log and asserted their 9/23 values. The game (started by the other chat) rewrote Options.ini at 01:44 with fullscreen=0 and windowedfullscreen=1, and the suite no longer passes. It would also break as soon as the user runs the recommended 'use-stock --apply'.
findings.evidence: Rerun at 01:49: OptionsTests.test_status failed (no windowedfullscreen note) and test_apply_only_listed_keys_and_restore failed (8 changes instead of the expected 9, windowedfullscreen missing). The builder reported 'Ran 21 tests ... OK'.
findings.fix: setUpModule now builds a fixed template. Options.ini keys are pinned to the 9/23 values. The SGR Full file comes from ConfigOverride or, after a real use-stock, from the newest copy in SpeedKit quarantine. SimpsSetters.sgr comes from the Setters folder, and MySetters.sgr is the user's own (or Ultimate Quality if theirs equals Ultimate Performance). Config.log is made to name SGR Full. Tests that need SGR Full skip with a reason if it cannot be found. The weak 'everything before stays identical' check in test_display_modes_extra_and_missing_key is now a line-by-line check.

findings.what: settings_sgr had no guard against include loops. A rules file that includes itself, directly or through another file, raised RecursionError. That crashed graphics_status, and because preflight only caught OSError/ValueError, it also crashed preflight() and launch().
findings.evidence: test_include_loop_is_an_error_not_a_crash and test_self_including_override_does_not_break_status_or_preflight both raised RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded before the fix.
findings.fix: Rules.run() now keeps a stack of files being read plus MAX_INCLUDE_DEPTH=16. A loop is recorded in Rules.errors at the include line. OSError, KeyError, ArithmeticError and RecursionError on a single line are now line errors too. preflight catches any exception from the graphics hint and adds a note.

findings.what: When an if/elseif condition could not be parsed, no frame was pushed. The body then ran as if the condition were true, and the next else/endif popped the outer frame, which inverted the outer branches for the rest of the file.
findings.evidence: test_bad_if_expression_keeps_nesting before the fix produced 3 errors (the parse error plus IndexError on 'else' and on 'endif'). It also set both inner_true and outer_else.
findings.fix: Added Rules._test(): a condition that cannot be run counts as false and is logged, so the nesting stays correct.

findings.what: When Options.ini already ends with a blank line, which the game's own file does, appended keys produced a triple CRLF. The docs claim keys are appended 'in the game's own style'.
findings.evidence:
Before the fix the output contained 'frameratelimit = 60


useuncompressedtextures = 0'.
findings.fix: _rewrite_options now writes 'key = v' followed by one blank line when the file ends with a blank line, and puts the blank line in front otherwise. Tests updated to match.

findings.what: options_apply only checked that values matched [A-Za-z0-9_.;-]+. It accepted True (written as 'True'), 'abc', simquality=9 and 6.5 for frameratelimit, so values the game does not know could be written into Options.ini.
findings.evidence: options_apply(extra={'simquality': 9}) and extra={'simquality': True} both produced plans with no error.
findings.fix: A value must now be a whole number (the regex \d+, bools rejected). For keys with levels it must be a known level from OPTION_INFO; these were checked against the stock rules, e.g. MaxProtectedSims 0-3. The integer is what gets written.

findings.what: If caches_clean got the same name twice, it tried to quarantine the file twice. It stopped mid-run with 'already quarantined' and left a 'failed' journal.
findings.evidence: test_duplicate_names_are_cleaned_once raised JournalError before the fix.
findings.fix: Names are deduplicated in order before planning.

findings.what: launch.detect_profile and settings._parked_state raised AttributeError when Mods_parked\_manifest.json was not an object with a 'moved' list. The other tool owns that file. Because of this, preflight() and launch() crashed instead of reporting 'unknown'.

findings.what: Smaller robustness and API gaps. options_status ignored an unknown preset without saying so. caches_status could raise if the Mods switch tool moved localthumbcache between listing it and reading its size. The 'settings restore' CLI without an id raised IndexError. launch() with a relative exe path passed cwd='' to Popen. graphics_status did not mention a missing include, such as Setters rules copied without SimpsSetters.sgr, whose values then silently read as 0.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code. test_value_checks (options_status('ultra') did not raise) and test_status_names_a_missing_include fail against the pre-fix code.
findings.fix: options_status raises ValueError for an unknown preset. File sizes use a _size() helper that returns 0 when the file is gone. The CLI prints usage and returns 2 when restore has no id. launch() takes os.path.abspath(exe). graphics_status adds notes for missing includes and for rules lines that could not be read.

findings.what: display='auto' rests on the premise that fullscreen=1 plus windowedfullscreen=1 is 'inconsistent', but the game wrote that state itself on 9/23. findings.what: The lag meter blamed script mods for EA's own code. `sampling._functions_of` recorded each wrapper's own `co_filename` when building the owner map. A `functools.wraps` decorator copies `__module__` from the mod's function, but the wrapper's code lives in the file that defines the decorator. Class members also had no `__module__` check. As a result EA's `T:\InGame\Gameplay\Scripts\Core\caches.py` was mapped to WickedWhims, which is in Mods now, and every EA cached test on the stack was charged to it. `areaserver.c_api_server_tick` is itself `@exception_protected` (in `sims4/utils.py`), so a mod with a module-level `@exception_protected` function would have been charged for every Python sample.
findings.evidence:
Read-only scan of the real archives:
- `Mods\scripts\TURBODRIVER_WickedWhims_Scripts.ts4script` has 10 classes (for example `IsFaithfulTest`, `WhiteRomanceTest`) with `@turbo_cached_test def __call__`, and `turbo_cached_test = caches.cached_test`.
- EA's `cached_test` and `exception_protected` both use `functools.wraps` (`core.zip` `caches.pyc` line 255, `sims4/utils.pyc` line 163).
- The same EA decorators appear in `lot51_core` (25 uses), `NisaK` (21), `DQuiet`, `FallenCore`, `HARKI`, and in `[Kuttoe] BasementalAddons` (`exception_protected`).

Reproduction:
- Under 3.12 the old map was `{'T:\InGame\Gameplay\Scripts\Core\caches.py': 'TURBODRIVER_WickedWhims_Scripts.ts4script'}`, and a stack of EA frames only was charged to WickedWhims.
- A scenario in the game's own `python37_x64.dll` (`tests/test_ingame_review2.py`) had a true split of 3.6% for the WickedWhims-like mod, 25% for game and 0% for the Kuttoe-like mod.
  - Old code: 19.5% / 0.8% / 11.1%.
  - Fixed code: 4.5% / 23.9% / absent.
findings.fix:
In `ingame/speedkit_monitor/sampling.py`:
- New `_own_function` follows the `__wrapped__` chain (with a cap of 20 steps) to the real function and skips wrappers of non-functions.
- The `__module__` check now covers class members, `staticmethod`/`classmethod` members and property parts, and accepts both the `sys.modules` key and `m.__name__`.
- `module_code_filenames` never returns a filename starting with EA's roots, `EA_CODE_PREFIXES` = (`T:\InGame\Gameplay\Scripts\`, `D:\dev\TS4\_deploy\`), taken from the research's `ea_cofilename.py`.

Seven 3.12 tests and one game-DLL test in `tests/test_ingame_review2.py` cover this. All of them fail on the old code.

findings.what: A bad `launch_time.json` silently disabled the whole mod for the session. `loadtimer.parse_time_value` let `OSError`/`OverflowError` out of `datetime.timestamp()`, which the game's 3.7 on Windows raises for naive dates before 1970 or far in the future. `__init__._start` ran `on_import`, `install` and `register` in one try block, so the load hooks, the cheats and the CC guard were never installed. The only trace was an `ERROR` line in `monitor.log`.
findings.evidence: In the game's DLL: `datetime.fromisoformat('1969-12-31T23:00:00').timestamp()`, `'0001-01-01'` and `'9999-12-31T23:59:59'` all raise `OSError [Errno 22]`. Reproduction on a fake tree: `on_import` raised `OSError [Errno 22] Invalid argument`. ISO-8601 is an accepted format in the documented `launch_time.json` contract.
findings.fix:
- `parse_time_value` now catches `(ValueError, OverflowError, OSError)` and returns `None`.
- `__init__._start` runs load-timer set-up, hook install and cheat registration as three separately guarded steps.

Tests:
- 3.12 tests check that the pre-1970 date is ignored, the hooks and cheats are installed and there is no `ERROR` in the log, and that a raising `on_import` does not cost the hooks or the cheats.
- The game-DLL scenario runs with a pre-1970 `launch_time.json` and gets 3 cheats and `launch_source` `config.log`.

findings.what: Nothing ended a lag run when its lot was unloaded. Only `Zone.update` (the deadline check) or the main menu could stop it. So faulthandler kept dumping all threads through a travel loading screen, where there are no ticks. That screen got mixed into the report, which was then labelled with the new lot. On quit-to-desktop it kept dumping into the game's shutdown, where reading frames without the GIL is the research's open crash risk.
findings.evidence:
- `simulation.zip` `areaserver.pyc` `request_client_disconnect_gen` line 462 calls `LOAD_METHOD on_teardown` on the zone for travel and quit, and `Zone.on_teardown(self, client)` is at `zone.pyc` line 791.
- Measured in the game's DLL: a 12,000-sample run with 3 extra threads makes a 95 MB dump, cut to 64 MB (8,562 samples) and parsed in 2.8 s.
findings.fix: `lagmeter.ensure_tick_wrapper` now also wraps `Zone.on_teardown`, pass-through and best effort; it only logs when the method is missing. That wrapper ends the run with 'lot unloaded' and `show=False`. `loadtimer.on_lot_loaded` then calls `lagmeter.show_pending()`, so the notification appears once after the next lot loads, titled '(previous lot)'. Tested under 3.12 and in the game's DLL (150 ticks, then teardown: report 'stopped by lot unloaded', no notification until the next lot, then exactly one).

findings.what: The lag report, `monitor.log` and `loadtimes.csv` were written as strict UTF-8. Mod names come from Windows file names, which can hold an unpaired surrogate. If one did, the report write in `_analyse` raised and the whole lag result was lost ('SpeedKit lag meter failed'). The log line or CSV row was dropped the same way.
findings.evidence: Both `LoneSurrogateTests` fail on the old code (the report and the log/CSV) and pass after the fix.
findings.fix: `errors='replace'` on the report write (`lagmeter._analyse`), in `common.log` and in `loadtimer.append_row`.

findings.what: A bug outside this component, in `speedkit/journal.py` (not edited). Journal ids have one-second resolution. Two journals of the same kind created in the same second share an id: the second overwrites the first's journal file and shares its quarantine folder. The first run's quarantined files are then not recorded in any journal, so they cannot be undone.
findings.evidence: Fake tree under `E:\speedkit_test\ingame_review\r2`: two `Journal('dedup')` objects in the same second both got id `20260924-023213-dedup`. `list_journals` showed only the second one. `undo` restored `b.package`, but `a.package` stayed in quarantine with no journal entry. `ingame_install` avoids this with `_free_journal_slot`; other components (dedup, profile) may not.
findings.fix: In `journal.py`, make the id unique: add milliseconds or a counter, or use `O_EXCL` creation with a suffix on collision.

findings.what: A bug outside this component, in `speedkit/library.py` (not edited): `game_running()` never closes its `os.popen` handle.
findings.evidence: `ResourceWarning: unclosed file` at `library.py:74` `os.popen('tasklist ...').read()`, seen in every install test run.
findings.fix: Use `with os.popen(...) as p:` or `subprocess.run`.

findings.what: `ingame_install` leaves its staging copy (`SpeedKit\staging\SpeedKit_Monitor.ts4script.<pid>.tmp`) behind when a run fails after the copy, for example when `put_new` is refused because the target appeared.
findings.evidence: The existing review test `test_file_that_appears_after_planning_is_never_overwritten` leaves the `.tmp` file in staging. It is outside Mods, so the game never loads it.
findings.fix: Left in place on purpose because of the never-delete rule. A later cleanup could quarantine or remove its own temp files.

findings.what: sanitize_name/build_flat could still produce names S4S cannot unmerge safely. (a) MAX_NAME counted code points, not UTF-16 units, so 200 emoji became 360 units, over NTFS's 255-unit name limit. (b) A lone surrogate made build_flat raise UnicodeEncodeError. (c) Uniqueness used str.lower() only, so pairs NTFS treats as the same file (ſ/s, ς/σ, ı/i) stayed distinct. S4S would then write both sources into one file, and one of them would be lost. (d) CONIN$, CONOUT$, COM¹-³ and LPT¹-³ were not treated as reserved names.
findings.evidence: On the original code: 'AssertionError: 360 not less than or equal to 180'; 'UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed'; 'sam' != 'sam (2)' for the pair ('ſam', 'sam'). On 3,000 random ASCII/Latin-1 manifests, build_flat and rewrite_without output is byte-identical before and after the fix, so dedup's inputs are unaffected.
findings.fix: New fold_name() (each character upper-cased on its own like NTFS, then lower-cased), used by sanitize_name(taken) and check_names; _cap() limits names by UTF-16 units; _BAD_CHARS now includes \ud800-\udfff; the reserved-name set is extended.

findings.what: When a file's size and mtime matched a file seen earlier, its fingerprint was taken over without reading it (meant for backup rotation), even when that other file was still in place. The game writes whole-second mtimes, so a new Tray/save file sharing size and mtime with an existing one took over the other file's fingerprint and was never parsed. Its CC was then silently missing from the pack.
findings.evidence: Stats only, on the real folders: 188 of 409 save/Tray files have whole-second mtimes, and 2 (size, mtime) groups already collide. test_new_file_sharing_size_and_mtime_with_one_still_there_is_read fails on the original code: Family B's part 0xA7000000000000FF is not found.
findings.fix: _fingerprint_sources now takes over a fingerprint only when the old path no longer holds a file with that size and mtime (a real rename). A rename-based rotation still costs no read (test_rotation_by_rename_takes_the_fingerprint_over_without_reading).

findings.what: _scan_job checked only size and mtime after parsing. A same-size, same-second rewrite between fingerprinting and parsing would be cached under the old fingerprint. After a scan error the stale 'seen' row stayed, so the same wrong fingerprint was reused on the next scan.
findings.evidence: test_save_changed_after_fingerprint_is_not_cached_under_it and test_a_scan_error_forgets_the_fingerprint.
findings.fix: The worker now hashes the exact bytes it parses and compares them with the expected fingerprint (_fingerprint_bytes). On error the path's 'seen' row is deleted so the file is fingerprinted afresh next time.

findings.what: The pattern ('RD', 5, 17) for HouseholdData.cas_inventory matched only an unpacked varint. The game's own schema (generated.zip) declares it 'repeated uint64 [packed=true]', so the pattern could never match. No current impact: the research hit table has no RD.5.17 values in any of the 44 saves, and the schema parse of Slot_18 finds 0 entries.
findings.evidence: Dumped with the game's descriptors: 'HouseholdData 17 repeated uint64 cas_inventory packed=True'. test_packed_cas_inventory_is_read fails on the original code. Cross-check against the schema on Slot_00000018 and a .ver3 copy: sculpt 287/287, genetic sculpt 238, modifiers 780, tones 58, rewards 6,111, thrift 271, custom colours 2, all with 0 misses (other patterns are correct).
findings.fix: Added (('RD', 5, 17, 0), PART_OTHER). SCANNER_VERSION changes, so used_refs.sqlite is re-parsed once.

findings.what: build() and _source_entries could fail with FileNotFoundError when the other tool moved a source package to the other root after _check_sources but before the copy opened it. On any failure the source handles were not closed (leaked until GC).
findings.evidence: test_package_moved_to_the_other_root_before_it_is_copied fails on the original code with FileNotFoundError. In that failed run, rmtree could not delete Mods_parked/cc/A_first.package, which was still held by the leaked handle (the leftover t_gxcgqv1n folder).
findings.fix: _find_source/_open_source look the package up again at the same relative path in the other root (same size and mtime). The source handles are closed in both the success and failure paths. os.makedirs(staging) moved inside the try, so the journal cannot stay 'open'.

findings.what: max_package_bytes had no upper bound, so a caller could produce packages over 2 GiB, which have never been seen loading in-game (research verdict loadorder 13 is UNCERTAIN). An out_dir inside saves/ or Tray/ was refused only by the Journal at the move stage, after the whole copy had been staged.
findings.evidence: test_packages_over_2_gib_are_refused (original: 'ValueError not raised'). test_out_dir_in_saves_is_refused_before_any_work (original: JournalError only after staging).
findings.fix: layout() raises ValueError when max_package_bytes > 2^31-1. build() refuses an out_dir in saves/Tray before any journal or staging.

findings.what: verify() of a pack built with .ver backups, given refs scanned without backups, silently skipped the backup ids and could report 'complete'.
findings.evidence: refs.ids(cat, True) only covers fingerprints in by_fp, which excludes unscanned backups. Covered by test_verify_of_a_backup_pack_needs_backup_refs.
findings.fix: verify() raises ValueError in that case, the same guard plan() has.

findings.what: test_game_ids_cached passed without testing anything. It compared info['built'], which has one-second resolution, and the fake game rebuilds in milliseconds, so a rebuilt cache also passed.
findings.evidence: tests/test_usedpack.py test_game_ids_cached.
findings.fix: The test now writes a marker row into the cache's meta table (a rebuild wipes it) and checks it survives. The review test also checks that a changed game package mtime triggers a rebuild.

findings.what: NOT FIXED (outside this component): speedkit/dbpf.py Package() and library.py Library.scan() open packages with plain open(). Any component that keeps a Package open for long blocks the game's renames and mods_switch.py's moves in the same way as the critical finding.
findings.evidence: The same WinError 32 test (plain handle vs FILE_SHARE_DELETE handle) as the critical finding. usedpack no longer uses Package for saves or sources, but other components do.
findings.fix: Suggest a shared share-delete opener in dbpf.py (like usedpack._open_read) and using it in Package and Library.scan.

findings.what: NOT FIXED (journal.py): undo() cannot resume a partial undo. If one reversal succeeded and a later one failed, a second undo() refuses outright, because the check phase requires every quarantined copy to still exist. usedpack's rollback relies on undo.
findings.evidence: Demo under E:\speedkit_test\usedpack_review\jr: after one quarantine step was restored, undo raised 'quarantined copy is missing: ...\b.package' and a.package was never restored.
findings.fix: In journal.undo, skip steps whose effect is already reversed (for example, path exists and q is missing) instead of refusing.

usedpack.tests_after: python tests/test_usedpack.py -> "Ran 15 tests in 8.844s" / "OK"; python tests/test_usedpack_review.py -> "Ran 20 tests in 5.698s" / "OK" (the new file has 20 adversarial tests on fake trees under E:\speedkit_test\usedpack_review. Run against a scratch copy of the ORIGINAL usedpack.py, 16 of them gave "FAILED (failures=6, errors=8)": WinError 32 on save rotation and package move, no rollback, empty game-id cache, missed packed cas_inventory, no 2 GiB guard, FileNotFoundError for a moved package. The later fingerprint-collision test also fails on the original.) Old and new scan_file results are identical on the real save/Tray copies in E:\speedkit_test\usedpack\fake_sims (8 files). A read-only real plan() with the fixed code (private copy of the library index, 2 real save copies + 6 Tray copies) gave 7,972 keys, 0.674 GB from 152 source packages, 26 households with missing CC, 52,465 game CASP copies read with 0 errors, and all sources unchanged, in 11.6 s.
remaining_risks: The cas_inventory pattern fix changes SCANNER_VERSION, so the next scan_references() re-parses every save and Tray file once (~96 s current, ~290 s more with backups). I did not re-scan the real saves (the game was running), so data/used_refs.sqlite is still the builder's and will be invalidated on first use. load_refs()/plan() will refuse until that rescan.

Packed varint lists (sculpts, thrift inventory, cas_inventory) are read as packed only when the blob does not also parse as a protobuf message. Measured 0 of 230 multi-sculpt blobs affected and 0 misses vs the schema on real saves, but an EA-id-first list could in principle hide ids.

Residual windows: a save is still held open for the ~0.1-0.3 s it takes to fingerprint or read it. With FILE_SHARE_DELETE a rename works, but replacing the file while it is open (MoveFileEx onto it) still fails with WinError 5 (tested).

A build killed outright (no exception handler) leaves up to ~7 GB of staging under SpeedKit\staging and an 'open' journal. Rolled-back new pack files are kept under SpeedKit\quarantine\<id>\_undone_new (disk use). The rollback runs undo(check_game=False), which moves only SpeedKit's own pack files.
journal.undo is not resumable after a partial undo (finding, not fixed). dbpf.Package and Library.scan still use plain handles (finding, not fixed).
mods_switch.py (the other tool) still reacts badly to any locked file (copy + failed unlink, manifest not saved), whatever process holds the lock (antivirus, other components).
The full 7 GB pack has still not been built from real data, and in-game behaviour is still unverified: CASP fallbacks, first-copy-wins for CC on 1.126, packages over 2 GiB.
